entry.title: Research Summary: June 24, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by safety/alignment and agentic AI, alongside a standout clinical deployment and a foundational theory contribution.

Clinical & applied impact: RaDaR, an open-source 32B reasoning LLM for rare disease diagnosis, anchors the day with a randomized AI-physician-assistance trial validating real-world deployability.

Safety & alignment (the strongest theme):

  • RL Towards Broadly Beneficial Models tests whether beneficial-behavior RL generalizes broadly and persistently across realistic multi-domain data.
  • Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process decomposes misalignment into 18 cognitive indicators with activation-based linear probing.
  • Self-Recognition Finetuning offers a mechanistic defense that prevents and reverses emergent misalignment across GPT-4.1 and Qwen2.5-32B.
  • RIFT-Bench introduces graph-driven dynamic red-teaming for agentic AI security.

Agents, interpretability & foundations:

  • OpenThoughts-Agent delivers a fully open agentic data-curation pipeline with 100+ controlled ablations.
  • AgenticInterpBench/HyVE benchmarks LLM agents as circuit explainers in mechanistic interpretability.
  • Bareinboim's Causal Reinforcement Learning introduction unifies causal inference and RL over counterfactual relations.

Theory & training dynamics: The Geometry Behind Diffusion and Flow Matching elegantly unifies both under Wasserstein-space gradient flows and geodesics, while a plasticity-loss study probes whether scale rescues continual learning in 5M–314M parameter transformers.

entry.title: A specialized reasoning large language model for accelerating rare disease diagnosis: a randomized AI physician assistance trial

author.name: Haichao Chen, Songchi Zhou, Zhengyun Zhao, Shikai Hu, Xianghong Jin, Hongwei Ji, Li He, Shuli Li, Yiming Qin, Xin Tan, Runfeng Shi, Yih Chung Tham, Jiaye Zhu, Ye Li, Ye Jin, Longhao Cao, Dawei Li, Honghan Wu, Hongqiu Gu, Guanqiao Li, Tudor Groza, Chunying Li, Dian Zeng, Weihong Yu, Gareth Baynam, Saumya Shekhar Jamuar, Min Shen, Shuyang Zhang, Bin Sheng, Sheng Yu, Tien Yin Wong

entry.summary: RaDaR is an open-source compact 32B reasoning LLM for rare disease diagnosis, trained on 49,170 real free-text cases plus 104,666 synthetic reasoning-enhanced cases, evaluated in a randomized AI physician assistance trial and outperforming larger open models including 671B DeepSeek. It matters for addressing scarce specialized expertise in timely rare disease diagnosis through a deployable model with clinical validation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Towards Broadly and Persistently Beneficial Models

author.name: Akshay V. Jagadeesh, Rahul K. Arora, Khaled Saab, Ali Malik, Mikhail Trofimov, Foivos Tsimpourlas, Johannes Heidecke, Karan Singhal

entry.summary: This paper studies whether reinforcement learning on beneficial behaviors in realistic domains can produce broad and persistent alignment generalization beyond training distribution, constructing a dataset to measure traits like truthfulness, fairness, and corrigibility. It matters because RL can introduce reward hacking and deception, and the authors test whether beneficial-behavior RL generalizes out of distribution.

entry.title: Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process of Language Models

author.name: Kaiwen Zhou, Constantin Venhoff, Jonathan Michala, Xin Eric Wang, William Saunders

entry.summary: This paper proposes monitoring LLM misalignment by decomposing it into 18 fine-grained cognitive indicators (such as deception, sandbagging, self-preservation) and detecting them in internal activations via linear probes, with an out-of-distribution evaluation. It matters for reliably detecting misaligned behaviors in high-stakes deployments through interpretability-based monitoring.

entry.title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models

author.name: Negin Raoof, Richard Zhuang, Marianna Nezhurina, Etash Guha, Atula Tejaswi, Ryan Marten, Charlie F. Ruan, Tyler Griggs, Alexander Glenn Shaw, Hritik Bansal, E. Kelly Buchanan, Artem Gazizov, Reinhard Heckel, Chinmay Hegde, Sankalp Jajee, Daanish Khazi, Emmanouil Koukoumidis, Xiangyi Li, Hange Liu, Shlok Natarajan, Harsh Raj, Nicholas Roberts, Ethan Shen, Nishad Singhi, Michael Siu, Ashima Suvarna, Hanwen Xing, Patrick Yubeaton, Robert Zhang, Leon Liangyu Chen, Xiaokun Chen, Steven Dillmann, Saadia Gabriel, Xunyi Jiang, Anurag Kashyap, Boxuan Li, Yein Park, Minh Pham, Sujay Sanghavi, Lin Shi, Ke Sun, Yixin Wang, Zhiwei Xu, Erica Zhang, Siyan Zhao, Wanjia Zhao, Jenia Jitsev, Alex Dimakis, Benjamin Feuer, Ludwig Schmidt

entry.summary: OpenThoughts-Agent provides a fully open data curation pipeline for training broadly capable agentic models, with over 100 controlled ablation experiments revealing the importance of task sources and diversity, and a 100K-example training set. It matters because little is publicly known about curating training data for agents that generalize across diverse agentic tasks rather than a single benchmark.

entry.title: The Geometry Behind Diffusion and Flow Matching: Gradient Flows and Geodesics in Wasserstein Space

author.name: Yian Yao, Weiwei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper unifies diffusion and flow matching under the geometry of Wasserstein space, showing that the forward diffusion process descends the free energy and each denoising step realizes one JKO scheme step, recovering DDPM, DDIM, NCSN/SMLD, and energy matching as one scheme. It matters for providing a unified theoretical lens on generative modeling methods.

entry.title: Self-Recognition Finetuning can Prevent and Reverse Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Arush Tagade, Shaoheng Zhou, Jiaxin Wen, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Proposes self-generated text recognition finetuning as a character-targeted defense against emergent misalignment, testing across GPT-4.1, Qwen2.5-32B, and Seed-OSS-36B. Finds it can both prevent and reverse misalignment by reinforcing the model's aligned persona rather than directly suppressing harmful content.

entry.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

author.name: Ayan Antik Khan, Harsh Kohli, Yuekun Yao, Huan Sun, Ziyu Yao

entry.summary: This paper introduces AgenticInterpBench and HyVE, an agentic explainer that interprets identified circuit components through iterative observation, hypothesis generation, and causal validation. It matters because mechanistic interpretability has automated circuit localization but explaining component function remains labor-intensive and hard to standardize.

entry.title: An Introduction to Causal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Elias Bareinboim, Junzhe Zhang, Sanghack Lee

entry.summary: This is an introduction to causal reinforcement learning, articulating how causal inference and RL both operate over counterfactual relations and proposing their integration. It matters for unifying two largely independent disciplines around counterfactual reasoning to improve agents' decision-making.

entry.title: RIFT-Bench: Dynamic Red-teaming For Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Yarin Yerushalmi Levi, Roy Betser, Amit Giloni, Lidor Erez, Itay Gershon, Oren Rachmil, Sindhu Padakandla, Roman Vainshtein

entry.summary: RIFT-Bench introduces a graph-representation-driven methodology for dynamic red-teaming of agentic AI systems, enabling unified security evaluation across heterogeneous architectures via a two-phase discovery and adaptive-attack scanning process. It matters because agentic LLM systems expose new attack surfaces beyond traditional LLM vulnerabilities, and existing evaluations are implementation-specific.

entry.title: Can Scale Save Us From Plasticity Loss in Large Language Models?

author.name: J. Fernando Hernandez-Garcia, Tom\'as Figliolia, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: This work studies plasticity loss in GPT-style transformers (5M to 314M non-embedding parameters) on a multilingual continual learning problem, finding evidence of plasticity loss persists and asking whether scale can overcome it. It matters because plasticity loss is a fundamental obstacle to continual learning, understudied in modern transformer LLMs and natural-language domains.

entry.title: One Year Later...The Harms Persist, But So Do We!

author.name: Annika Marie Schoene, Cansu Canca, Gautham Vijay Kumar, Anson Antony

entry.summary: Evaluates safety safeguards of six proprietary LLMs across 16 DSM-5 mental health conditions using adversarial attacks, introducing an eight-dimension harm taxonomy. Finds safeguards reliable only for suicide and self-harm, with failure rates up to 100% for eating disorders and substance use.

entry.title: Red-Teaming the Agentic Red-Team

author.name: Dario Pasquini, Michal Bazyli, Taras Fedynyshyn, Artem Sorokin

entry.summary: This work presents the first in-depth security analysis of widely used agentic systems for offensive cybersecurity, showing common design flaws that let an adversary exfiltrate API keys, establish persistence, and compromise the operator's machine even inside sandboxes. It introduces a full cyber kill chain against these red-teaming agents.

entry.title: Safe and Generalizable Hierarchical Multi-Agent RL via Constraint Manifold Control

author.name: Zihao Guo, Jianing Zhao, Ling Li, Hao Liang, Giuseppe Loianno, Yali Du

entry.summary: This work proposes a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that enforces hard safety constraints at the low level via a constraint manifold while enabling coordination through high-level policy learning, with theoretical safety guarantees. It addresses the trade-off between empirically strong learning methods and conservative control-theoretic safety in multi-agent settings.

entry.title: Bayesian control for coding agents

author.name: Theodore Papamarkou, Vladislav Smirnov, Viktor Mazanov, Artem Vazhentsev, Preslav Nakov, Timothy Baldwin, Artem Shelmanov

entry.summary: This paper formulates coding-agent orchestration as cost-sensitive sequential hypothesis testing, with a Bayesian controller maintaining a belief over candidate correctness and dynamically deciding whether to gather evidence, refine, verify, or stop. It matters because tool-use decisions in coding agents typically use fixed rules ignoring uncertainty, and the belief state also yields an interpretable correctness score.

entry.title: Cyclic Denoising Reveals Ultrastable Memories in Diffusion Models

author.name: Rishabh Sharma, Stefano Martiniani

entry.summary: This paper introduces cyclic denoising as an extraction attack for image diffusion models, performing repeated forward-reverse diffusion at controlled noise amplitudes to expose ultrastable attractors largely inaccessible to standard sampling. Many of these attractors correspond to memorized training images including stock photos and watermarks, requiring only sampler-level control without gradients.

entry.title: Beyond Trajectory Imitation: Strategy-Guided Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Tianyuan Shi, Canbin Huang, Bei Li, Xin Chen, Xiaojun Quan, Jingang Wang, Qifan Wang

entry.summary: Strategy-Guided Policy Optimization (SGPO) replaces instance-level trajectory imitation with reusable strategy distillation, extracting structured strategy descriptions from strong models and comparing autonomous versus strategy-guided trajectories. It matters because trajectory imitation encourages memorization rather than transferable reasoning skills, limiting generalization in distilled models.

entry.title: The Latent Bridge: A Continuous Slow-Fast Channel for Real-Time Game Agents

author.name: Bojie Li, Noah Shi

entry.summary: The Latent Bridge couples a slow reasoning VLM and a fast reactive VLM for real-time game agents, learning a continuous latent communication channel between two frozen models as the sole trainable component, replacing the standard text bridge. It matters for real-time computer-use agents that must act within milliseconds while planning over seconds.

entry.title: Solving Inverse Problems of Chaotic Systems with Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Peiyan Hu, Jian Zhang, Jiashu Pan, Ruiqi Feng, Tao Zhang, Zhi-Ming Ma, Yuan-Sen Ting, Gongjie Li, Tailin Wu

entry.summary: Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching (Bi-CFM) solves inverse problems in chaotic systems—inferring initial conditions from final states—by learning bidirectional mappings between initial and final state distributions, with a conservation-constrained extension, tested on Lorenz, Circuit, and Lorenz 96 systems. It matters because chaotic inverse problems are largely unsolved due to ill-posedness, non-uniqueness, and instability.

entry.title: Weight-Space Geometry of Offline Reasoning Training

author.name: Aleksandr Nikolich, Igor Kiselev, Vladimir Platonov, Karina Romanova

entry.summary: Mechanistically compares six offline reasoning-distillation losses (SFT, RFT, DFT, RIFT, Offline GRPO, DPO) via weight-space geometry analysis using LoRA on Qwen3-4B. Finds SFT, RFT, and RIFT produce nearly colinear weight updates, suggesting some methods are mechanistically equivalent.

entry.title: Large-Language-Model Discovery of Quantum LDPC Codes through Structured Concept Evolution

author.name: Zidu Liu, Florian Marquardt

entry.summary: This work introduces structured concept evolution, pairing an LLM with an algebraic mutation grammar to discover lifted-product families of quantum LDPC error-correcting codes rather than designing codes from first principles. It evolves structured algebraic specifications to tackle a challenging discrete design problem.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 23, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans foundational RL theory, embodied AI, scientific modeling, and a heavy concentration of safety and security findings.

Theory & Foundations

  • Inverting the Bellman Equation (Foerster et al.) proves value-based RL agents trained across rich reward sets implicitly encode a unique, accurate world model, bridging model-free and model-based RL.
  • Unsupervised disentanglement work shows local Jacobian orthogonality enforces identifiability, challenging long-standing impossibility intuitions for nonlinear generative models.

Embodied & Scientific Models

  • NVIDIA's Vesta (Fan, Kautz, Zhu) unifies localization, spatial reasoning, navigation, and long-horizon planning into a single embodied generalist foundation model.
  • Atomistic Language Models (MIT, Gomez-Bombarelli) combine an atomistic encoder, LLM, and denoising diffusion for SOTA materials understanding and generation.
  • GEOPHYS (Simoncelli, Torr, Laptev, Klindt) captures physical plausibility via five geometric properties of frozen image-encoder embeddings, validated against EEG.

Safety & Security

  • Knowledge editing does not truly erase facts; edited knowledge resurfaces under adversarial elicitation, with mechanistic analysis exposing the illusion of erasure.
  • A preregistered 2,610-participant study finds warning labels shift perceptions of sycophantic AI but fail to reduce its actual influence.
  • Import AI 462 reports a ~19,000-conversation study showing AI reliably out-persuades expert humans on politically charged topics.
  • The Watermark Shortcut shows provenance watermarking sabotages audio deepfake detectors, which latch onto watermarks rather than synthesis artifacts.
  • A mechanistic account links prompt injection success to how chat-template tags encode conversational roles in the residual stream.

entry.title: Inverting the Bellman Equation: From $Q$-Values to World Models

author.name: Alistair Letcher, Mattie Fellows, Alexander D. Goldie, Jonathan Richens, Jakob N. Foerster, Oliver Richardson

entry.summary: This paper proves that value-based RL agents trained over a sufficiently rich set of reward functions implicitly encode a unique, accurate world model, and introduces P-learning to extract that model as an inverse of Q-learning. It bridges the model-free versus model-based dichotomy with theoretical conditions on goal/reward diversity.

entry.title: Vesta: A Generalist Embodied Reasoning Model

author.name: Johan Bjorck, Zhiqi Li, Yunze Man, Jing Wang, An-Chieh Cheng, Sifei Liu, Shihao Wang, Zhiding Yu, Abhishek Badki, Stan Birchfield, Valts Blukis, Yevgen Chebotar, Siyi Chen, Sicong Leng, Yu-Cheng Chou, Tianli Ding, Boyi Li, Zhengyi Luo, Hang Su, Jonathan Tremblay, Tingwu Wang, Bowen Wen, Jimmy Wu, Xianghui Xie, Hanrong Ye, Hongxu Yin, K. R. Zentner, Liangyan Gui, Yu-Xiong Wang, Yuke Zhu, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Jan Kautz

entry.summary: Vesta is a unified embodied generalist foundation model from NVIDIA that consolidates localization, spatial reasoning, navigation, and long-horizon planning into a single model with a multimodal memory harness. It beats individual SOTA baselines by over 20% on average across diverse benchmarks.

entry.title: GEOPHYS: The Geometry of Physical Plausibility

author.name: Christian Intern\`o, Alexander Pondaven, Habon Issa, Fabio Pizzati, Francesco Pinto, Markus Olhofer, Ivan Laptev, Philip Torr, Eero P. Simoncelli, Barbara Hammer, David Klindt

entry.summary: GEOPHYS argues that physical plausibility is implicitly captured by five geometric properties of frozen image-encoder embeddings, enabling fast physics-violation detection that correlates with human EEG responses. It claims SOTA without MLLM judges or training modifications.

entry.title: Warning labels shift perceptions of sycophantic AI, but not its influence

author.name: Lujain Ibrahim, Myra Cheng, Cinoo Lee, Pranav Khadpe, Desmong Ong, Dan Jurafsky, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: A preregistered experiment with 2,610 participants tests whether warning labels mitigate sycophantic AI's influence in interpersonal-conflict discussions. Labels shift perceptions (reducing trust and perceived objectivity) but do not reliably reduce sycophancy's actual influence on judgment.

entry.title: Exposing the Illusion of Erasure in Knowledge Editing for LLMs

author.name: Advik Raj Basani, Anshuman Chhabra

entry.summary: Demonstrates that knowledge editing in LLMs does not truly erase facts; edited knowledge resurfaces under adversarial elicitation. Mechanistic analysis shows low-rank updates redistribute rather than overwrite knowledge, acting as suppression rather than deletion.

entry.title: Atomistic Language Models Understand and Generate Materials

author.name: Sathya Edamadaka, Krithik Ramesh, Ju Li, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: Introduces Atomistic Language Models that unify a pretrained atomistic encoder, an LLM, and a denoising diffusion model so a single backbone can understand structures, generate materials from text, and optimize crystals. Achieves SOTA on crystal structure prediction and de novo generation.

entry.title: Import AI 462: Superpersuasion; self-sustaining AI; paths to ASI

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter highlights a large study (nearly 19,000 conversations) finding AI systems are reliably more persuasive than expert humans on policy and donation decisions, even when humans prepared extensively and were incentivized. It also covers self-sustaining AI and paths to ASI.

entry.title: Unsupervised Disentanglement Without Compromises : How Functional Orthogonality Enforces Identifiability

author.name: Mathieu Cyrille Simon, Pascal Frossard, Christophe De Vleeschouwer

entry.summary: This paper proves that imposing local orthogonality on the Jacobian of the generative mapping yields identifiability of general nonlinear generative models without statistical independence or causal assumptions, given a full factor-combination domain. Experiments with orthogonality-regularized normalizing flows confirm reliable factor recovery.

entry.title: The Watermark Shortcut: How Provenance Marking Sabotages Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Nicolas M. M\"uller, Pascal Debus

entry.summary: Reveals that provenance watermarking of synthetic speech creates a spurious shortcut where deepfake detectors latch onto watermarks rather than learning genuine artifacts. Identifies three failure modes including watermarked fakes evading detection and real watermarked voices being flagged as fake.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Explanation of Prompt Injection (and why you should study roles)

author.name: Charles Ye

entry.summary: Presents a mechanistic theory that prompt injection succeeds because of how LLMs encode conversational roles via chat template tags, using this to construct new attacks and explain interpretability findings. The authors advocate for a new research subfield studying the science of roles.

entry.title: Protein contacts are already in the attention: a single-forward-pass alternative to the Categorical Jacobian

author.name: Rome Thorstenson

entry.summary: This work shows protein contact signals reconstructed by the Categorical Jacobian (about 19L forward passes) are already concentrated in a small subset of attention heads, recoverable in a single forward pass by averaging top-K contact-relevant heads selected on as few as 10 labeled proteins. It matches or beats CJ across bidirectional protein language models.

entry.title: MuPPET: A Benchmark for Contextual Privacy of LLM Assistants in Multi-Party Conversations

author.name: Elena Sofia Ruzzetti, Cornelius Emde, Sangdoo Yun, Seong Joon Oh, Martin Gubri

entry.summary: Introduces MuPPET, a benchmark testing whether LLM assistants leak private information in multi-party conversations like group chats, where one disclosure reaches all members at once. Finds models leak substantially more in multi-party settings than single-interlocutor ones, exposing an unmeasured privacy risk.

entry.title: Discretizing Reward Models

author.name: Vijay Viswanathan, Shiqi Wang, Devamanyu Hazarika, Chirag Nagpal, Tongshuang Wu, Graham Neubig, Yuning Mao

entry.summary: Shows that continuous-scoring reward models are often oversensitive, assigning different scores to equally good responses, which can lead to bad RL policies. Proposes discretizing reward models, with theoretical and empirical support.

entry.title: Superhuman AI for Generals.io Using Self-Play Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Matej Straka, Viliam Lis\'y, Martin Schmid

entry.summary: Presents a superhuman self-play RL agent for Generals.io, a real-time imperfect-information strategy game, reaching #1 on the 5000+ player leaderboard and beating top humans. A key enabler is a JAX-native simulator achieving roughly 10,000x speedup over prior tools.

entry.title: Brittle model organisms obstructs deception elicitation work

author.name: Advik

entry.summary: Shows that finetuning-based auditing methods for deception model organisms can inadvertently erase the very hidden behaviors they aim to measure, producing an illusion of success. Using secret side constraint organisms, the authors find models stop following hidden constraints while still claiming to, inflating intervention effectiveness.

entry.title: ConnectomeBench2: A Unified Benchmark for Automated Connectomic Proofreading

author.name: Jeff Brown, Tim Farkas, Gleb Razgar, Edward S. Boyden

entry.summary: ConnectomeBench2 releases a unified multi-species dataset of over 716,000 expert-labeled proofreading decisions with 4.5 million images across mouse, human, zebrafish, and fly connectomes, and trains a single Vision Transformer reaching human-level accuracy for split error correction and merge identification. Targets the rate-limiting proofreading step in connectomics.

entry.title: Detecting Malicious Agent Skills in the Wild using Attention

author.name: Bacem Etteib, Daniele Lunghi, T\'egawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: Presents Locate-and-Judge, an attention-based two-stage detector for malicious agent skills—third-party instruction packages that execute with user privileges. Argues prompt-injection defenses fail here because skills are themselves trusted instructions.

entry.title: Learning through Internalization

author.name: Nikolaos Tsilivis, Nirmit Joshi, Marko Medvedev, Julia Kempe, Nati Srebro

entry.summary: Studies internalization processes by which transformers absorb explicit chain-of-thought procedures into their weights, examining which semiautomata are harder to internalize and the resulting degradation of out-of-distribution performance. Provides the first provable analysis of successful internalization for learning parities.

entry.title: Massive Activations Are Architecturally Robust: A Controlled Scratch/Commitment Residual Stream Test

author.name: Maruthi Vemula (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)

entry.summary: Tests whether massive activations in transformers are removable artifacts of residual stream overloading by introducing Ledger Residuals that split the stream into a mutable scratch and protected accumulator. Finds massive activations remain, suggesting they are architecturally robust and functional.

entry.title: Safe to Check, Unsafe to Use: Relinking at the Compression Boundary of LLM Agents

author.name: Zesen Liu, Zihan Zhang, Dongdong She

entry.summary: This paper identifies relinking, a compression-boundary vulnerability where summarization-based prompt compressors act as confused deputies, combining distributed benign fragments into a complete malicious instruction. Unlike prompt injection, no explicitly malicious payload need appear in the source.

entry.title: The Language-Energy Divide: Measuring Energy Costs of Multilingual LLM Inference

author.name: Naihao Deng, Alissa Shen, Yiming Feng, Joan Nwatu, Jae-Won Chung, Mosharaf Chowdhury, Yulong Chen, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: This systematic study measures inference energy across languages, finding per-output-token energy varies up to 8.3x and total energy for fixed requests up to 179x between English and Pashto. The disparity is driven by higher per-token costs for complex scripts and more tokens needed per content.

entry.title: Learning Process Rewards via Success Visitation Matching for Efficient RL

author.name: Raymond Tsao, Andrew Wagenmaker, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Proposes transforming sparse outcome rewards into dense process rewards by training a discriminator between successful and unsuccessful episodes, then incentivizing the policy to match successful state-action visitations. Addresses credit assignment for efficient RL.

entry.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report

author.name: Yujin Tang, Edoardo Cetin, Jinglue Xu, Qi Sun, Stefan Nielsen, Vincent Richard, Haruto Goda, Iaroslav Tymchenko, Nhan Nguyen, Hyunin Lee, Mari Ashiga, Shashank Kotyan, So Kuroki, Tarin Clanuwat

entry.summary: Sakana Fugu is a family of orchestrator models trained to understand queries and dynamically devise agentic scaffolds that coordinate a team of specialized LLM agents, achieving state-of-the-art results beyond any individual agent. Aims to combine the specializations of different frontier LLMs into a collective system.

entry.title: Towards Understanding the Power and Limits of the Muon Optimizer: A River-Valley Perspective

author.name: Tianqi Shen, Jinji Yang, Runze Shi, Jianhao Ma, Jiaye Teng, Ziye Ma

entry.summary: Develops a trajectory-level theory using a mixed-spiked matrix sensing model to explain when the Muon optimizer outperforms Adam and when its gains are mixed in LLM training. Provides a river-valley loss-landscape perspective on Muon's strengths and limits.

entry.title: Local Causal Attribution of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Dennis Wei, Yannis Belkhiter, Erik Miehling, Radu Marinescu

entry.summary: Proposes AttriCoT, a black-box method that builds a structural causal model over units of a chain-of-thought trace to attribute each unit's causal influence on output log-probabilities using O(U) forward passes. Aims to improve transparency and safety of LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Naturally learned behaviors in deep MLPs resist detection by both human and learned algorithms

author.name: emanuelr

entry.summary: Investigates whether secrets memorized by MLPs can be recovered from weights or black-box queries, a toy version of eliciting hidden behaviors in LLMs. Finds that hard-negative training plus depth makes memorized secrets resistant to input-optimization attacks, while learned weight-readers only modestly help.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 22, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment, spanning one empirical benchmark and several conceptual threat-model contributions.

  • MonitoringBench is the standout: a difficulty-graded benchmark of 2,644 successful attack trajectories for evaluating monitors that oversee coding agents, shipped with released code. It is the only item with original empirical work and practical tooling.
  • A high-level model of AI bargaining applies open-source game theory to how advanced AIs could use credible commitments unavailable to humans, a novel theoretical framing for AI conflict and cooperation.
  • A misalignment taxonomy organizes alignment failures into five kinds of inner misalignment, including *precocious misalignment* from half-baked subgoals—a useful conceptual scaffold.
  • How persona training could fail argues persona-trained models could develop genuine internal goals during RL, connecting persona methods to deceptive-alignment risk.

Remaining items are weaker or off-topic. Policy changes should be rolled out gradually makes a software-deployment analogy for governance but lacks AI specificity. The rest—a Cookie Monster AI-safety metaphor, a Google calculator parsec unit bug, and a board-game recommendation—are outreach or recreational content with no novel research substance.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 18, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety, interpretability, and evaluation integrity, alongside notable advances in robotics and RL.

Deception and lie detection drew the most substantive work:

  • "Did you lie?" builds belief-verified model organisms to rigorously evaluate LLM lie detectors, addressing a key methodological pitfall.
  • Rift controls for incorrectness to isolate an internal conflict signature distinguishing deliberate deception from honest errors.
  • STATEWITNESS trains a separate decoder to read hidden states and produce natural-language deception audits.

Evaluation reliability is a recurring theme:

  • Several frontier models are substantially prefill aware, undermining the validity of widely-used prefill-based safety evaluations.
  • SAE Interventions are Unreliable shows suppressed unsafe behavior can be recovered post-intervention, questioning SAE-based safety steering.
  • Vision-language models for chest radiography exposes that medical VLMs often exploit text priors rather than reading images.
  • A Position paper on coding benchmarks argues current scores conflate model, harness, and environment, misaligning with agentic software engineering.

Architecture and learning advances:

  • KV Cache as editable notebook demonstrates causally that cached key/value vectors store memoized conclusions, with practical composability implications.
  • Reversal Q-Learning (Park, Levine) bridges flow matching and off-policy Q-learning via an expanded MDP over refinement steps.
  • Do as I Do retargets monocular human videos to multi-fingered robot hands, scaling dexterous manipulation data.
  • Nothing from Something probes whether LLMs can discover the concept of zero, a conceptually deep OOD-generalization case study.

  • Vision-language models for chest radiography exposes that medical VLMs often exploit text priors rather than reading images.
  • A Position paper on coding benchmarks argues current scores conflate model, harness, and environment, misaligning with agentic software engineering.

Architecture and learning advances:

  • KV Cache as editable notebook demonstrates causally that cached key/value vectors store memoized conclusions, with practical composability implications.
  • Reversal Q-Learning (Park, Levine) bridges flow matching and off-policy Q-learning via an expanded MDP over refinement steps.
  • Do as I Do retargets monocular human videos to multi-fingered robot hands, scaling dexterous manipulation data.
  • Nothing from Something probes whether LLMs can discover the concept of zero, a conceptually deep OOD-generalization case study.

entry.title: “Did you lie?” Evaluating Lie Detectors across Model Scale and Belief-Verified Model Organisms

author.name: Alan Cooney

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM lie detectors by building belief-verified model organisms that demonstrably hold a belief contrary to what they state, plus a prompted-lying testbed. Finds that activation- and logprob-based detectors scale positively when lying is prompted but drop sharply when lying is trained in, casting doubt on current detectors' reliability.

entry.title: Rift: A Conflict Signature for Deception in Language Models

author.name: Petr Nyoma

entry.summary: Rift investigates whether deception leaves an internal signature in LLMs by contrasting a sleeper agent that lies on trigger against a naive liar producing identical wrong answers. It finds deceptive passes carry a conflict signature with higher residual rank, enabling lie identification with 100% accuracy and no labels.

entry.title: SAE Interventions are Unreliable: Post-Intervention Recovery of Suppressed Behavior

author.name: Mingyue Cui, Linghui Shen, Xingyi Yang

entry.summary: Shows that interventions on sparse autoencoder features intended to suppress unsafe model behavior are unreliable, because the behavior can be recovered via residual-space optimization even after clamping. This challenges latent-space safety defenses that assume SAE features are actionable handles for control.

entry.title: Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos

author.name: Bhawna Paliwal, Haritheja Etukuru, William Liang, Pieter Abbeel, Nur Muhammad Mahi Shafiullah, Jitendra Malik

entry.summary: DO AS I DO reconstructs and retargets monocular RGB human videos to multi-fingered dexterous robot hands, recovering hand-object interactions from in-the-wild egocentric and exocentric sources. It aims to unlock abundant RGB-only human video as scalable dexterous manipulation data.

entry.title: Models Take Notes at Prefill: KV Cache Can Be Editable and Composable

author.name: Bojie Li

entry.summary: This work shows that an LLM's KV cache acts like a notebook of memoized conclusions, where a field's own key/value vectors drive under 1% of downstream decisions. This enables editable and composable caches, allowing field corrections via chain-of-thought at roughly 1% compute.

entry.title: Decoding Hidden Deception in Reasoning LLMs: Activation Explainers for Deception Auditing

author.name: Kexin Chen, Yi Liu, Haonan Zhang, Yanhui Li, Xinyu Deng, Dongxia Wang

entry.summary: STATEWITNESS is an activation explainer for deception auditing that uses a separate decoder to read a target model's hidden states and produce natural-language reports about suspicious behavior. It reaches 0.916 mean AUROC across seven deception datasets, outperforming black-box and probe baselines.

entry.title: Reversal Q-Learning

author.name: Aditya Oberai, Seohong Park, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Reversal Q-Learning is an off-policy RL algorithm that trains a flow policy on prior data using an expanded MDP treating flow refinement steps as actions, generating virtual on-policy trajectories by reversing flows. It applies bias-and-variance reduction to mitigate the curse of horizon.

entry.title: Self-CTRL: Self-Consistency Training with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Itamar Pres, Laura Ruis, Melat Ghebreselassie, Belinda Z. Li, Jacob Andreas

entry.summary: Self-CTRL trains language models so their self-explanations and actual behavior remain consistent, by reinforcement learning that updates either explanations or behavior. Tested on probabilistic reasoning tasks, it improves the correlation between self-reported and measured biases, supporting auditability and trust.

entry.title: EDoF-NeRF: extended depth-of-field neural radiance fields using a coded aperture camera

author.name: Yoshiyuki Shirasaki, Ryoichi Horisaki

entry.summary: SC3-Eval adapts a pretrained video foundation model into an accurate robot policy evaluator by enforcing forward-inverse dynamics, multi-view, and out-of-distribution consistency. It offers a scalable alternative to expensive real-world policy evaluation.

entry.title: Several frontier models are substantially prefill aware

author.name: yeedrag

entry.summary: Extends UK AISI work on prefill awareness, showing several frontier models can distinguish tampered assistant-side content from genuine content even under conservative elicitation and in low-stakes settings. This matters because prefill-based methods underpin many safety evaluations (jailbreaking, persona, introspection), and awareness could confound pre-deployment safety claims.

entry.title: Pulling The REINS: Training-Free Safety Alignment of Video Diffusion Models via Representation Steering

author.name: Rohit Kundu, Arindam Dutta, Sarosij Bose, Athula Balachandran, Amit K. Roy-Chowdhury

entry.summary: REINS is a training-free safety alignment method for video diffusion models that steers internal representations toward safe generation at inference time. It finds safety-relevant structure is linearly encoded and that a single PCA-derived direction separates safe from unsafe content.

entry.title: Predicting LLM Safety Before Release by Simulating Deployment

author.name: Tomek Korbak

entry.summary: Describes a deployment simulation method for forecasting how a new model will behave before release by replaying prior conversations in a privacy-preserving way with the candidate model. In a GPT-5.4 study it predicted the direction of behavior change 92% of the time for categories shifting by 1.5x or more, far above a 54% baseline.

entry.title: Synthetic document finetuning for instilling positive traits

author.name: CallumMcDougall

entry.summary: A DeepMind interpretability team research update on instilling positive traits in Gemini 3 Flash via synthetic document midtraining followed by synthetic chat finetuning, building on Marks et al and Li et al. They report the chat finetuning robustly instills traits that generalize out-of-distribution and share practical takeaways for improving effectiveness.

entry.title: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report

author.name: Jaehun Jung, Ximing Lu, Brandon Cui, Muhammad Khalifa, Shaokun Zhang, Hao Zhang, Jin Xu, Amala Sanjay Deshmukh, Karan Sapra, Andrew Tao, Yejin Choi, Jan Kautz, Mingjie Liu, Yi Dong

entry.summary: ProCUA-SFT introduces a 3.1M-sample synthetic dataset for training computer-use agents, generated through an automated pipeline that synthesizes grounded desktop tasks. It addresses the negative transfer problem where the largest public dataset (AgentNet) actually degrades agent performance during fine-tuning.

entry.title: First Proof Second Batch

author.name: Mohammed Abouzaid, Nikhil Srivastava, Rachel Ward, Lauren Williams

entry.summary: Tests several AI systems on ten research-level mathematics problems arising naturally in working mathematicians' research, providing problems, methodology, human and AI solutions, and referee reports. Assesses current AI's ability to solve genuine open-ended math research.

entry.title: Spokes: Optimizing for Diverse Pretraining Data Selection

author.name: Clarence Lee, Yejin Choi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Pang Wei Koh, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: Introduces Spokes, a probabilistic diversification framework using the G-Vendi score optimized via exponentiated gradient descent to directly optimize set-level diversity in pretraining data selection. It produces substantially more diverse subsets than random sampling, improving performance under fixed data budgets.

entry.title: Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention in Hybrid Architectures

author.name: Ziqing Qiao, Yinuo Xu, Chaojun Xiao, Zhou Su, Zihan Zhou, Yingfa Chen, Xiaoyue Xu, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic analysis of hybrid LLM architectures combining full attention with efficient modules (sliding-window attention, recurrent mixers), examining scaling behavior, mechanism, and design. It finds efficient-attention design mainly affects how fast long-context capability emerges while hybrids converge to similar performance with enough training.

entry.title: Nothing from Something: Can a Language Model Discover 0?

author.name: Phoebe Zeng, Thomas L. Griffiths, Brenden M. Lake

entry.summary: Investigates whether language models can independently discover the mathematical concept of zero, using arithmetic as a case study for out-of-distribution mathematical generalization. Frames mathematical discovery as requiring strong novel-structure hypothesis generation.

entry.title: How Inference Compute Shapes Frontier LLM Evaluation

author.name: Jessica McFadyen, Ole Jorgensen, Harry Coppock, Kevin Wei, Cozmin Ududec

entry.summary: Evaluates up to 12 frontier LLMs on seven hard benchmarks (software engineering, math, medicine, cybersecurity) under controlled inference-scaling interventions (token budgets, context compaction, repeated sampling). Shows that single restrictive compute budgets can understate true model capability.

entry.title: Vision-language models for chest radiography do not always need the image

author.name: Mahshad Lotfinia, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Lisa Adams, Daniel Truhn, Andreas Maier, Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh

entry.summary: Introduces a causal audit that intervenes on chest X-ray images to test whether vision-language models actually use the image rather than exploiting finding-name priors. Strikingly, a text-only model comes within 5.7 accuracy points of the best multimodal model, exposing a fundamental evaluation flaw.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ralf R\"omer, Maximilian Seeliger, Saida Liu, Ben Sturgis, Marco Bagatella, Daniel Marta, Andreas Krause, Angela P. Schoellig

entry.summary: Proposes a method to quantify epistemic uncertainty in flow-matching vision-language-action models by measuring velocity-field disagreement across a small ensemble, enabling detection of unreliable robot actions out of distribution. This addresses a critical safety gap for deploying VLAs in real-world non-stationary environments.

entry.title: Retrievable Gradients: Continual Post-Training Without Cumulative Weight Drift

author.name: Weihang Su, Jiacheng Kang, Jingyan Xu, Qingyao Ai, Jianming Long, Hanwen Zhang, Bangde Du, Xinyuan Cao, Min Zhang, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: Proposes ReGrad, a paradigm treating gradients as retrievable knowledge units: precomputing document-specific gradients offline into a Gradient Bank and retrieving query-relevant gradients at inference for temporary weight adaptation, avoiding cumulative weight drift. It aims to combine RAG's drift-free property with deeper parametric knowledge integration.

entry.title: The Value Axis: Language Models Encode Whether They're on the Right Track

author.name: Nick Jiang, Isaac Kauvar, Jack Lindsey

entry.summary: This work investigates whether language models internally track the value of their current trajectory, constructing a value axis for Qwen3-8B that distinguishes high versus low confidence, backtracking, and correct versus corrupted code. Steering along this axis causally suppresses or induces self-correction and exploration, and DPO can increase the internal value of rewarded behaviors.

entry.title: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework

author.name: David Huang, Jaewon Chang, Avidan Shah, Prateek Mittal, Chawin Sitawarin

entry.summary: Rapid Poison demonstrates practical poisoning attacks against the Rapid Response framework used in production safety systems including Anthropic's ASL-3, showing prompt injection can deliver poisoned samples into the jailbreak-classifier training set to create targeted false positives and concept-based backdoors. It exposes a real vulnerability in continuous safety-classifier improvement pipelines. Significant for production AI safety.

entry.title: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents

author.name: Sina Hajimiri, Masih Aminbeidokhti, Jose Dolz, Ismail Ben Ayed, Issam H. Laradji, Spandana Gella, Nicolas Gontier

entry.summary: Re-evaluates online memory, workflow, and skill modules for web agents under a fixed inference-token budget, finding a token-matched vanilla baseline matches or beats AWM, ASI, and ReasoningBank across WebArena domains and three models. It questions whether augmentation modules justify their token overhead.

entry.title: Tying the Loop -- Tied Expert Layers in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: Expert Tying is an architectural modification for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs that shares expert parameters across consecutive transformer layers while preserving independent layer-wise routing and attention. Pretraining experiments on OLMoE, Qwen3, and DeepSeek-style MoEs show nearly 2x memory reduction at virtually no perplexity or downstream degradation.
